## The Problem: The Hashing-Indexing Tax

Every KV system pays a hidden cost: hashing and indexing. Lookups require hash computation, collision resolution, and tree traversals. As data grows, p99 latency degrades, caches thrash, and indexes amplify writes 10x–50x — wasting storage and demanding continuous DBA tuning.

The KV market's leading products prove the limits of this paradigm, not its health. Redis's triple-license model (AGPLv3/RSALv2/SSPLv1) has driven 75% of users to seek alternatives.[^redis] Valkey forks BSD code but inherits the same architecture. In July 2026, an autonomous AI agent discovered 19 Redis zero-days — one became a working RCE exploit in 27 minutes. Some vulnerabilities remained unfixed for seven months.

**The root cause is structural:** hash tables destroy locality, indexes amplify writes, and scripting layers multiply attack surfaces. The market does not need a faster Redis or a safer fork. It needs a way out of the hashing-indexing paradigm entirely.

## The Solution: Eliminate Hashing and Indexing

CoordStore removes the root cause — hashing and indexing themselves.

- **No hash functions** → No collisions to resolve. No rehashing. No resize pauses.
- **No indexes** → No B-trees to traverse. No LSM compaction. No write amplification.
- **No scripting engine** → No Lua VM. No module loader. No RDB parser. Attack surface = arithmetic only.

Every operation is a single arithmetic step — no lookups, no traversals, no hash probes. The result is deterministic, predictable performance at any scale.

## Storage Model: Projection, Not Logging

CoordStore projects data directly onto storage — no write-ahead log, no compaction, no garbage collection.

- **No WAL** → Nothing to replay on crash.
- **Instant Recovery** → Crash recovery is a memory remap (milliseconds), not log replay (minutes to hours).[^recovery]
- **Write Amplification = 1x** → SSD lifespan extends proportionally.

| Metric | CoordStore | Traditional | Advantage |

| Single get (string key) | **22.5 ns** | 23.8 ns | 1.1× |

| Batch get (1K keys) | **2.26 µs** | 22.76 µs | 10× |
| Latency vs scale | **21.5 ns flat** | +19% at 10M | Scale-free |
| Prefix scan (nonexist) | **1.65 ns** | 23.05 ms | 14.0M× |
| Multi-axis (3 axes) | **94 ns** AND | 13 µs scan | 138× |
| Spatial proximity | **96–353 Melem/s** | N/A | New capability |
| 125M keys memory | **119 MB fixed** | ≥200 MB | Exact planning |

> p99 = p50. Performance is deterministic across all scales.

## Key Differentiators

- **Zero collisions** — deterministic addressing, no collision resolution.
- **No resizing** — fixed memory footprint; no pause-the-world events.
- **Predictable latency** — O(1) across all scales, no GC, no compaction jitter.
- **Spatial queries** — Proximity search, bounding box, distance metrics as primitive operations. No hash-based system can replicate this — a hash digest has no spatial structure; a CoordStore coordinate is an address with embedded geometry.
- **No attack surface** — No Lua VM, no module loader, no RDB deserializer. Just arithmetic.
- **Hardware ready** — 300-gate decoder specification for ASIC/FPGA.

## The Unfair Moat

CoordStore is not an algorithmic tweak; it is a **structural discovery** that competitors cannot replicate by tuning existing approaches. While others optimize hash functions, cache policies, or index algorithms, CoordStore eliminates the underlying hash-index paradigm entirely.

Open-core (Apache 2.0) timestamps priority; enterprise layers (persistence, networking, security) are commercial.

## Pure Software, Global Scale

CoordStore is a pure software layer — no hardware supply chain, no MOQs, no logistics. Deployable on cloud, on-prem, or hybrid — immediate global distribution. IP licensing to semiconductor manufacturers is an optional high-margin channel.

## Strategic Summary

CoordStore is not a faster hash table or a safer database fork. It is a structural replacement for hashing and indexing themselves — the first fundamental change to the KV indexing layer since the hash table.

Every operation is deterministic: no collisions, no resizing, no compaction. O(1) across all scales. External events (license shifts, zero-day exploits) accelerate the market's need. But CoordStore stands on its own: arithmetic, not hashing. Coordinates, not tables. O(1), not O(log N).
